series: Walkthrough for the bank Short str-july-242-november-104.json, built Oct 7, 2026 for CMO review
hook: A $185 base rate means $242 a night in July
hook_say: This video shows how to set Airbnb and VRBO nightly rates by season, using one base rate and your own last 12 months of revenue.

rows.label: Base nightly rate
rows.why: Start with the base nightly rate, the price for an average month. The example cabin uses $185.

rows.label: July revenue, last year
rows.why: Next, type in what each month brought in over the last 12 months. July brought in $5,600, and the average month was $4,275.

rows.label: July multiplier
rows.why: Divide July by the average month and July runs at 1.31 times normal. That multiplier sets the July price.

rows.label: July nightly rate
rows.why: $185 times 1.31 is $242 a night for July. The busy month is priced for the demand it already has.

rows.label: November revenue, last year
rows.why: November brought in only $2,400, so it runs at 0.56 times an average month.

rows.label: November nightly rate
rows.why: The same math puts November at $104 a night, and April lands at $113. Both are low enough to need a limit.

fix.label: Your $115 floor holds November at
fix.why: That limit is the floor. Set it at $115 and no month is priced below it: November and April both hold at $115.
